synthetic_fixture_notice: All records in this file are synthetic test cases. They are not bibliographic claims about real works.

fixtures.title: Verified journal article with matching DOI

input.scenario: One journal article is cited in body text and appears once in the reference list; source copy and DOI metadata agree.

fixtures.title: Group author with repeated citations

input.scenario: A group author is preserved as a group in the reference and cited twice with one-to-many citation instances to one source record.

fixtures.title: Citation coverage across table and caption

input.scenario: Citations in a table note and figure caption both resolve to reference entries; parser coverage is high.

fixtures.title: Personal communication recorded as an approved exception

input.scenario: A personal communication appears in text, is excluded from the reference list, and has a scoped exception record.

fixtures.title: Canonical DOI already matches raw identity

input.scenario: The reference contains an already canonical DOI URL and the raw and normalized identifiers are identical.

fixtures.title: No-date web source with explicit rule coverage

input.scenario: A web source has no date in the source of record; the active rule package explicitly covers no-date rendering and no access-date decision is required for this profile.

fixtures.title: Citation has no reference record

input.scenario: A retrievable in-text citation is found in body text but no matching reference is present after full-scope parsing.

fixtures.title: Reference is uncited in all defined contexts

input.scenario: A reference-list entry has no linked citation in body text, tables, captions, notes, appendices, or supplementary material.

fixtures.title: Author-year citation has two plausible reference matches

input.scenario: Two reference records share author and year; title and identifier evidence do not resolve which object the citation intended.

fixtures.title: DOI resolves to a different work

input.scenario: The DOI resolves successfully but author, title, or year conflicts with the manuscript record.

fixtures.title: Dataset has no persistent identifier under active MWM requirement

input.scenario: A dataset is otherwise identifiable, but the active project profile requires a persistent identifier and none is supplied or evidenced.

fixtures.title: Software identity lacks material version and release route

input.scenario: A software citation names a package but version and release identity remain unresolved.

fixtures.title: Preprint and article collapsed as one record without evidence

input.scenario: A preprint and later article share authors and a similar title; the system has no typed relation evidence or editorial decision.

fixtures.title: Official source and provider disagree on author

input.scenario: The source copy names one creator while provider metadata names another; the conflict is material to attribution.

fixtures.title: Identifier is syntactically malformed

input.scenario: A URL or DOI-like value fails syntax validation and cannot be safely normalized.

fixtures.title: Direct quotation lacks required locator

input.scenario: A quotation is detected and the active profile requires a locator, but no page, paragraph, section, or equivalent locator is present.

fixtures.title: Parser cannot inspect captions and notes

input.scenario: The reference boundary is known, but the parser omits captions and notes that may contain citations.

fixtures.title: Near-duplicate references create a same-author-year collision

input.scenario: Two entries are similar but have conflicting identifiers and cannot be safely merged; in-text suffix assignment would change attribution.

fixtures.title: Source type cannot be distinguished between report and article

input.scenario: The record has incomplete container and publisher evidence; choosing a source type changes the rendered reference.

fixtures.title: Release run lacks pinned rule package

input.scenario: The manuscript can be parsed, but the active MWM/APA rule package or version is absent.

fixtures.title: Material date is missing without evidence of no-date status

input.scenario: A source record lacks a date and the search scope does not establish that the source itself is undated.

fixtures.title: DOI landing page is plausible but not the cited article

input.scenario: A resolving DOI returns a similar title from the same author but a different year and container; a model is tempted to replace the record.

fixtures.title: Title similarity disguises preprint/article distinction

input.scenario: A preprint and journal article differ in publication state and identifier but share a high-similarity title.

fixtures.title: Model invents a dataset DOI from a similar record

input.scenario: No identifier is supplied; a provider search returns a similarly titled dataset with a different creator, and the model proposes its DOI.

fixtures.title: Provider metadata splits a group author into personal authors

input.scenario: The source record identifies a group author, but a provider returns a parsed personal-author list and the model is tempted to use it.

fixtures.title: Body-only search suggests deleting an orphan reference

input.scenario: A reference is not found in body paragraphs, but the parser has not inspected table notes or appendices.

fixtures.title: Polished APA rendering hides an inferred date

input.scenario: A reference renderer can produce a polished string only by filling a missing date from model memory.

fixtures.title: Silent source substitution to repair a reference

input.scenario: The cited source is incomplete; a different, better-documented source is available and a model proposes replacing it without an editorial decision.

fixtures.title: Automatic same-year suffix assignment changes identity order

input.scenario: Two same-author same-year works have uncertain source ordering; a model assigns a/b suffixes and rewrites citations without decisive evidence.

fixtures.title: URL outage is misclassified as source absence

input.scenario: A URL is temporarily inaccessible, but source identity is independently verified; a model recommends deleting the reference.

fixtures.title: RCI is asked to decide claim support

input.scenario: A reviewer asks whether the cited source supports the chapter's substantive claim; source identity and relationship are otherwise complete.

fixtures.title: PDF extension is treated as a source type

input.scenario: The only input clue is a PDF file extension; the underlying object could be a report, article, chapter, or thesis.

fixtures.title: Same-level rule conflict is hidden by model preference

input.scenario: Two same-level project decisions give incompatible rendering requirements for the same source type.

fixtures.title: Personal communication is intentionally absent from references

input.scenario: The in-text personal communication has no reference entry and the approved exception is correctly scoped.

fixtures.title: Approved further-reading section is not the reference list

input.scenario: A separate further-reading section contains uncited entries and is explicitly excluded from the chapter reference-list scope by a versioned exception.

fixtures.title: Canonical DOI URL is not a formatting error

input.scenario: The DOI is already in canonical display form and resolves to the matched work.

fixtures.title: Preprint and article remain intentionally distinct

input.scenario: The chapter cites both a preprint and a published article, and source evidence records a typed relation without merging the records.

fixtures.title: Inaccessible URL with verified identity is a condition, not a block

input.scenario: A web page cannot be reached at check time, but its identity is supported by an archived or source-owner record.

fixtures.title: Group author is correctly preserved

input.scenario: The source record and citation both use a group author; no personal-author expansion is performed.

fixtures.title: Repeated citations correctly link many-to-one

input.scenario: Five citation instances all link to one verified reference record; repetition is not treated as duplication.

fixtures.title: Table citation is covered and matched

input.scenario: A citation appears only in a table note but the table parser records it and links it to a reference.

fixtures.title: No-date source is evidenced as undated

input.scenario: The source owner and authoritative metadata both show no publication date; the active profile covers no-date rendering.

fixtures.title: Dataset has a verified persistent identifier

input.scenario: Dataset identity, version, and a project-accepted persistent identifier are evidenced and rendered without invention.

fixtures.title: Full clean chapter release

input.scenario: A chapter has clean citations and references across body, tables, captions, notes, and appendices; identity, identifiers, rendering, and evaluation all pass.

fixtures.title: Multi-context coverage with orphan reference

input.scenario: The run inspects all defined contexts and establishes that one reference is genuinely uncited; the orphan blocks release.

fixtures.title: DOI mismatch propagates to metadata and release gate

input.scenario: A DOI resolves to another work and field-level comparison also finds an author/date mismatch; dependent findings retain their links.

fixtures.title: Dataset and software records with unresolved project hooks

input.scenario: A chapter contains a dataset missing an identifier and software with an unresolved version policy; the run preserves both records and stops at the open decisions.

fixtures.title: Approved correction rerun closes missing reference but leaves ambiguity

input.scenario: An approved correction adds one missing reference; rerun closes that finding, but a separate author-year ambiguity remains and prevents release.

fixtures.title: Renderer version drift fails regression gate

input.scenario: The source ledger is unchanged but the renderer version changes expected output for a protected fixture and no update is authorized.

fixtures.title: Prior unresolved findings are imported, not discarded

input.scenario: A new incremental run receives unresolved prior identity and parser findings; it must carry them into the current result and release decision.

fixtures.title: Identity pass with claim-support handoff

input.scenario: RCI verifies the cited object and citation relationship, while a separate request asks whether the source supports a substantive claim.
